verbalization: Dofequidar is implicated in the targeting of UDP-glucuronosyltransferase 2B10, which in turn acts as a target for 9-Isovaleroxy Balanophonin. This chain of interactions suggests a potential mechanism by which Dofequidar influences the activity of the Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B1. The evidence points to a possible indirect relationship, where Dofequidar may modulate the expression or function of UDP-glucuronosyltransferase 2B10, which then affects the transporter. The integration of these pathways highlights a possible role for Dofequidar in regulating the activity of the transporter through a series of enzymatic and transport-related mechanisms. The relationship is supported by a clear, albeit indirect, sequence of targets, underscoring the complexity of drug-target interactions in this context.
